_comment: These overrides are SECURITY FLOORS for transitive dependencies. Each value must be at or above the advisory's patched version — a floor below it silently stops enforcing anything, because >= permits an upgrade without compelling one. That is exactly how fast-uri, @hono/node-server and postcss stayed vulnerable here while an override for each was already present. When you clear an advisory, raise the floor to the patched version rather than relying on a re-resolve. nanoid is the one floor with an upper bound, and it must keep it: an override REPLACES the consumer's range, so a bare >=3.3.17 would resolve to nanoid 6, which is ESM-only, while its only consumer here is postcss, which reaches it through require('nanoid/non-secure'). Cap it below 4 and the advisory is still fixed. Do not 'tidy' the <4 away.
